assertion.statement: For the retained global, primitive and derivative Selmer models, finite detecting evaluations give an H1 injection preserved by coefficient extension; their bounded outer quotient is a characteristic-zero DVR with uniformizer2, carrying the retained duality maps and approximate cycles as actual crossed homomorphisms.
assertion.objects: Actual retained cochain maps, product Galois groups, bounded finite detecting lists, primitive/derivative local conditions and O_infinity formed from valuation-bounded ring instances.
assertion.hypotheses: Fixed bounded minimal-model ranks, omega(k_j)≤A and a fixed number of derivative labels; retained evaluations and compatibility homotopies. Direct Selmer evaluation requires residual H0 isomorphism and H1 injection for the local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every indicated coefficient extension and each sequence of the bounded ring instances; evaluation at arbitrary sequences of group elements.
assertion.parameter_range: Primitive and derivative models with the stated local conditions. Orthogonal zero/full models only after an actual contraction at the chosen test ring.
assertion.uniformity: Detecting lists have bounded length at most dimV+dimW, selected and padded before the common limit. No support-uniform rank beyond the stipulated bound.
assertion.constants: Uniformizer2; no quantitative rank bound is added beyond the retained (5.1) bound.
assertion.normalizations: O_infinity is the ultraproduct quotient by sequences whose 2-adic valuation tends to infinity. Cochain evaluation uses the same ultrafilter, full compatibility homotopies and integral minimal-model inverses.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No continuity claim on one original Galois group and no completeness claim for the outer DVR. Zero local conditions may contribute evaluation-invisible H1, so direct injection is not asserted there. Approximate cycles are not silently replaced by exact finite-stage cycles.
assertion.limit_order: Choose finite detecting lists and cone cancellations before the common inner limit; form the bounded outer quotient; pass actual matrices and homotopies; only then regard differential-tending-to-zero sequences as crossed homomorphisms.
